title: Elements 1-18: the first three rows of the periodic table
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: The first eighteen elements are the ones you meet most: the air you breathe, the water you drink, the salt on the table and the sand on the beach. Learn these and the shape of the whole periodic table starts to make sense.

How to hold it: Eighteen is too many to hold at once, so take it a row at a time: row 1 has two elements, rows 2 and 3 have eight each, and the engine splits each row into two chunks of four. Picture each row as a shelf in your kitchen, and put a vivid object for each element on it, left to right (a balloon for helium, a battery for lithium, a diamond for carbon). Say the symbols out loud as you walk the shelf, then look away and rebuild it.
